topic: The Pi-Collision Mystery: From Physics to Mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Elastic Collision Paradox
lecture_lines: Two blocks of different masses collide elastically.
One block hits another and a wall.
Velocities change based on momentum and energy.
animations: Fade in text: Two colliding blocks of unequal mass.
Animate: Two blocks moving towards each other, then rebounding.
Highlight: Compare velocities before and after the collision.
Display MathTex: 'm_1 v_{1i} + m_2 v_{2i} = m_1 v_{1f} + m_2 v_{2f}' in white.
Flash: Energy conservation formula for the final state.

sections.title: Visualizing the Phase Space
lecture_lines: We map collision states into a 2D plane.
The particle trajectory shows the system's history.
animations: Define phase space grid with 'x_1' and 'x_2' axes.
Animate: Draw the trajectory line representing collision states.
Pulse: Highlight the intersection of the energy constraint ellipse.

sections.title: The Geometric Connection to Pi
lecture_lines: The trajectory path length links to geometry.
Reflections correspond to specific digits of Pi.
animations: Display unit circle to represent normalized energy constraints.
Animate: Count the number of total reflections in trajectory.
Overlay: Show pi digits corresponding to reflection sequence.

sections.title: Application and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Systems act as physical pi-calculating computers.
Conservation laws reveal deep mathematical constants.
animations: Final visualization of collision dynamics grid.
